summary:
We developed LunarSight, an interactive lunar mission-planning application that simplifies the evaluation and comparison of potential Moon landing sites, particularly near the lunar south pole. The platform visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to a selected landing location and date, helping users understand sunlight availability and direct-to-Earth communication opportunities.

LunarSight aims to provide an intuitive dashboard featuring landing site selection, date-based scenario comparisons, solar elevation, Earth visibility, and visual timelines of lighting and communication windows. By translating complex astronomical data into clear, accessible visualizations, it helps mission planners evaluate alternative landing scenarios quickly and efficiently.

This project addresses a critical challenge in lunar exploration: balancing scientific objectives with engineering requirements such as power generation and reliable communication. It is important because even small changes in landing location or mission timing can significantly affect operational feasibility. LunarSight bridges the gap between complex space-science tools and practical decision-making, making lunar exploration planning more accessible to engineers, educators, and the public.
details:
Project Details – LunarSight: Intelligent Lunar Landing Site Planner

LunarSight is an interactive lunar mission-planning platform designed to simplify the process of evaluating potential landing sites on the Moon, with a particular focus on the lunar south pole. It helps mission planners, researchers, educators, and space enthusiasts understand how the positions of the Sun and Earth affect power generation and communication opportunities at different landing locations and dates.

1. What does it do and how does it work?

LunarSight provides a user-friendly dashboard where users can select lunar landing locations, enter geographical coordinates, and explore different landing dates and times. The application visualizes the positions of the Sun and Earth relative to the local horizon.

It focuses on two critical mission requirements:

  • Solar Power Assessment: Displays solar elevation and sunlight availability to help estimate the potential for solar energy generation.
  • Communication Assessment: Shows Earth visibility to help identify potential direct-to-Earth communication windows.

The platform also supports comparing different landing scenarios, helping users understand how changes in location or landing dates affect mission conditions.

2. What are its benefits?

  • Simplifies complex astronomical information through intuitive visualizations.
  • Reduces the effort required to compare multiple landing scenarios.
  • Helps identify potential sunlight and communication constraints.
  • Supports faster preliminary mission-planning decisions.
  • Makes lunar exploration concepts understandable to non-specialists.

3. Intended impact

Our goal is to support safer, more efficient, and better-informed lunar mission planning. LunarSight can help engineering and science teams coordinate their requirements when selecting landing sites and mission dates. It also has educational potential, allowing students and the general public to explore the unique environmental challenges of lunar exploration.

4. Tools and technologies

The proposed technology stack includes:

  • Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript.
  • Visualization: Three.js for interactive celestial visualizations and Chart.js for displaying mission metrics.
  • Astronomical data: NASA/JPL Horizons for Sun and Earth ephemeris information.
  • Lunar data: NASA lunar surface and topographic datasets for geographical context.
  • Development tools: Visual Studio Code and Git/GitHub.

5. Creativity and innovation

The creative aspect of LunarSight is its focus on transforming complicated astronomical calculations into an intuitive, visual decision-support experience. Instead of requiring users to navigate multiple scientific tools and interpret raw datasets, it brings site selection, date exploration, Sun positioning, and Earth visibility into one interface.

6. Factors considered

During the design, we considered:

  • Extreme lighting variations near the lunar south pole.
  • Solar elevation and its relationship to solar panel performance.
  • Earth's visibility and communication opportunities.
  • The effects of landing location and mission date.
  • Lunar terrain and local horizon obstructions.
  • Accessibility for both technical and non-technical users.
  • The importance of reliable astronomical data and clearly communicating calculation limitations.

Overall, LunarSight aims to bridge the gap between complex space-science data and accessible lunar mission planning, helping make future lunar exploration more efficient, understandable, and adaptable.
